title: Fractal Semantic Graphs: Meaning Through Connectivity
note: The second edition of the argument the frozen first book made.
versioning: This book's version moves only when its content moves; the site's version moves on every push. v1.0.0 is reserved for the actual final release.

build.title: Fractal Semantic Graphs: Meaning Through Connectivity

parts.subtitle: The claim
parts.promise: Meaning through connectivity, from first principles, with no jargon before it is earned.

parts.subtitle: Semantic
parts.promise: What makes a graph semantic rather than merely a network: a grammar of verbs, anchors instead of standards, and types that are computed paths rather than applied labels.

parts.subtitle: Fractal
parts.promise: What the middle word of the title commits you to, how to falsify it, and what happens at every boundary and every zoom level once you take it seriously.

parts.subtitle: Computed
parts.promise: The half the first edition could not write: how a document becomes a graph anchored to bytes, what identity means when a document changes, an engine that computes meaning deterministically, and why an explanation is a path rather than a narration.

parts.subtitle: In practice
parts.promise: Where this runs today, what ships and what is argued, and how to build your own first graph tomorrow.

chapters.title: Fractal Semantic Graphs: Meaning Through Connectivity
chapters.blurb: What this book is, what you will know at the end, the editorial choices recorded, and the disclosure.

chapters.title: 1 · A node is just a node
chapters.blurb: The two 8080s, the five Reviews, the confidence ladder, and why a named absence beats a hidden one.

chapters.title: 2 · Why graphs at all
chapters.blurb: Three things people mean by graph and why this is the third; the positions on GraphRAG, RDF, property graphs and vector search; and the four situations where this argument is the wrong one.

chapters.title: 3 · Every edge is a verb
chapters.blurb: Five rules you can apply tomorrow, the banned edge, the fifteen verbs, and the register that makes the inverse rule machine-checkable.

chapters.title: 4 · Anchors, not standards
chapters.blurb: Why merging two vocabularies destroys the finding, the three-layer arrangement that replaces it, and two bridge registers you can watch being used.

chapters.title: 5 · A type is a path, not a label
chapters.blurb: Node type formulas, the grounding ladder, supersede-never-delete, and a compliance finding that is arithmetic.

chapters.title: 6 · Fractal is a testable claim
chapters.blurb: The zoom test, applied to this estate's own two zooms, including the row where it fails.

chapters.title: 7 · A graph at every boundary
chapters.blurb: Where determinism, explainability and provenance actually die, the security property stated narrowly, twins, and the air gap.

chapters.title: 8 · Documents are projections
chapters.blurb: The projection claim, and the build gate that rebuilds the document from the graph and fails unless the bytes match.

chapters.title: 9 · The universe method
chapters.blurb: How a raw document becomes a graph anchored to exact bytes, coverage total by construction, and the usage rating that caught the first edition misreading its own source.

chapters.title: 10 · Two kinds of address
chapters.blurb: Content address versus identity address, and a working algorithm for keeping identity stable across edits.

chapters.title: 11 · Meaning, computed
chapters.blurb: An engine in the shape of a transformer where nothing is learned and everything is named, with its formulas in the open and its limits stated.

chapters.title: 12 · Every box explains itself
chapters.blurb: Four properties an explanation must have to be checkable, and what happens when a diagram of a system is enforced by a test.

chapters.title: 13 · The fractal in production
chapters.blurb: Twenty published vaults, the worked graphs with real numbers, and what a network of nineteen sites does and does not demonstrate.

chapters.title: 14 · What ships, what is argued
chapters.blurb: What is running and checkable, what is a design, what does not exist anywhere, and four corrections this book carries.

chapters.title: 15 · Your first graph, tomorrow
chapters.blurb: An afternoon, a week and a month of instructions, ten rules on one page, and six ways this goes wrong.

chapters.title: Colophon: what was cut, and what remains open
chapters.blurb: How the book was made, what was cut, what remains open, where it might be wrong, and every figure with its source.

chapters.title: Reference card
chapters.blurb: The thesis, the ten rules, the edge set, the two ladders, the vocabulary, and the block to paste into an agent session.
